 (By Sri. R.V. Raghavendra Adv.,)
 2. The Manager,
 ICICI Lombard Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd.,
 No.121, 'D' Estate, Dickenson Road,
9th Floor, Bengaluru

(Insurer of the offending Car bearing  No.TS-08-FL-0052 vide policy  SCCH.13 3 MVC 4771/2021  No.3001/MI/10133177/00/000, valid  from 20-06-2021 to 19-06-2022)
 (By Smt.R Sharadamba Adv.,)
 JUDGMENT
This petition under Sec.166 of M.V.Act., is filed claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the original claimant Nagappa @ Nagaraj S/o. Lakshmaiah.
Thereafter, during pendency of petition, Petitioner Nagappa @ Nagaraj died and his LRs brought on record.

2. The brief facts of the case are that on 12- 10-2021 at about 3.15 p.m., Nagappa @ Nagaraj was a pedestrian near Sunkalamma Temple, Bagepalli Taluk, Chikkaballapura, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.TS-08-FL-0052 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against deceased/petitioner. Due to said impact,
Nagappa @ Nagaraj fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was taken to Bagepalli Government Hospital, he took first aid there.
Thereafter he was shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Even after continuous treatment, Nagappa @ Nagaraj has not recovered from accidental injuries and died on 20-04-2022.
The Petitioners have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food and nourishment, conveyances, attendant charges and other incidental charges.
The accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
3. Prior to the accident, the Nagappa @ Nagaraj was hale and healthy and was aged 58 years and earning his livelihood as a coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.

The Petitioners are the LRs of Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135304279/
2 deceased and are depending on the earnings of deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, they claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the Respondents with costs and interest from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
On the above grounds, they pray for allowing the petition.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsels and the respondent No.2 has filed the written statement.
The respondent No.1 has not resisted the case.
5. Respondent No.2 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
The respondent no 2 has denied all the averments of the petition and inter alia contending that there was no nexus between accidental injuries and death of Nagappa @ Nagaraj.

The alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased as he was influence of alcohol and without observing the vehicular movement and crossing the road.
The petitioner in active collusion with the police lodged false complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle drove the offending car without possessing valid driving license.
The owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions incorporated in the police.

Therefore, the respondent no 2 is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle. .
6.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues have been framed :
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that the death of Nagappa @ Nagaraj S/o.
Lakshmaiah was only due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.TS-08-FL-0052 on 12-10-2021, about 3.15 p.m., near Sunkalamma Temple, Bagepalli Town,
Chikkaballapura District?
2. What compensation Petitioners are entitled?
3. What order?
Additional issues:
1. Whether LRs of the petitioner proves that the petitioner died on account of accidental injuries?

2. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the said car without possessing valid driving license,
thereby the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions incorporated in the policy?
If so, whether the insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle?

Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135304279/
3 7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the claim, Lrs Petitioner No.2 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 17.
Further in support of their case, the Petitioners have examined 2 witnesses as PW- 2 and PW-3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.18 and Ex.P.19 respectively.

8. The Respondent No.2-insurance company has examined its official as RW-1 and authorization letter is marked as Ex.R.1.
9.

By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Addl.Issue No.1:
In the Negative Addl.
Issue No.2:
In the Affirmative Issue No.3:
11. In order to substantiate their claim, Lrs of the petitioner (b) has filed his affidavit in lieu of his examination in chief.
He has examined as PW-1.

Wherein he has deposed that on 12-10-2021 at 3.15 P.m., his father Nagappa was a pedestrian crossing the road near Sunkalmma temple, Bagepalli Taluk, Chikkaballapura, the driver of Car bearing No.TS-08- FL-0052 drove the same in a rash & negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, Nagappa fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was taken to Bagepalli Government hospital, he took first aid there.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and surgery was conducted for his left femur fracture and left knee fracture.
He discharged from the hospital after 10 days with advice to take follow treatment.
Nagappa died due to accidental injuries sustained to him.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
12. PW1 has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P1, complaint at Ex.P2, spot Mahazar at Ex.P.3, rough sketch at Ex.P.4,wound certificate at Ex.P.5 and charge sheet at Ex.P.6.
IMV report at EX.P.7.
On perusal of wound certificate, it shows that Nagappa has sustained left femur bone fracture and swelling over left orbital area.
13. Petitioners alleges that due to the accidental injuries Nagappa died.
PW-1 has stated that his father was inpatient for 10 days and surgery was conducted for his left femur fracture and left knee fracture .
He lost his earning capacity due to the accidental injuries.

Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135304279/
4 14.

entities.text: Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insurance company has contended that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident and the said vehicle was not caused any accident and driver of the offending car had not valid and effective DL.
There is a delay in registering the FIR.
On perusal of police records, it is found that there is a one day delay in registering the FIR.
But according to the medical records, he had admitted in the hospital with the history of RTA.

According to Ex.P5 - wound certificate of Govt.
hospital, Bagepalli, deceased Petitioner Nagappa had sustained left femur bone fracture and swelling over left orbital area and history of RTA is mentioned.

15. During the cross-examination, the learned counsel for the Respondent no 2 has put forth the suggestion that the accident was caused due to negligence of deceased Petitioner and false case was registered against the offending vehicle.
However PW1 has denied the same.
After 1 day FIR was registered and charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending car.
After through investigation IO has been filed charge sheet against offending vehicle.
Absolutely there are no contrary materials.
There are no materials to show that the insured car was not involved in the accident and it was not the negligence of driver of the offending car.
All the records corroborate with the evidence of Petitioner.
Hence I hold that Nagappa had sustained injuries in a RTA due to negligent driving by the driver of offending car.
The driver of offending car was negligent and it caused the injuries to Nagappa.
16. So far as the cause of death is concerned, LRs of the Petitioner say that the petitioner died on account of accidental injuries.
According to wound certificate, he had sustained left femur bone fracture and swelling over left orbital.
Femur bone fracture is shown as grievous in nature.
In the discharge summary shows that ORIF C ILN for left femur done.

At the time of discharge, he was advised regular wound dressing to be done, walker assisted mobilisation done and tablets and review.
17.
The learned counsel for petitioner has vehemently argued that there is nexus between the accidental injuries and death of Nagappa.
Due to accidental injuries, Nagappa was in continuous treatment and he died on account of accidental injuries.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent No,.2 vehemently argued that there is no nexus between the accidental injuries and death of Nagappa.
The LRs of petitioner have not produced any documents to substantiate that Nagappa died due to accidental injuries.
No PM report is produced and no FIR is registered for the offence punishalbe U/s.304(A) of IPC.
In the absence of PM report, the court cannot consider the death of Nagappa on account of accidental injuries.
18. Keeping in view of agruments addressed by the parties, once again I have perused the material available on record.
DR. S.A. Somashekar was examined as PW2 and he deposed that he was treated the deceased Nagappa in bowring hospital.
His condition was critical during the stay and he was suffering from fat embolism which is collection of fat in the lungs.
There was an open wound in the thigh and debridement and dressing was done.
He was discharged in stable condition.
He deposed that the accidental injuries might have contributed to the death of Nagappa as the injuries were severe.
During the cross-examination PW3 admitted that the deceased petitioner was discharged from their hospital, after completion of his treatment when the petitioner became relatively healthy and cured.

Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135304279/
5 19.

entities.text: Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The EX.P.13 death certificate shows that Nagappa died on 20/04/2022.
Except EX P8 and P14 treatment, till his death there are no other treatment taken by the deceased petitioner.
There are no medical bills either to show that he was continuously taking medicines or was under treatment.
20. The injuries shown in the discharge summary are not so severe to cause death of any person.
After the discharge he was at home for more than 6 months and died on 20/04/2022.
The cause of death is not known and he was not even taken to hospital before the death.
No postmortem report is conducted to prove that the death of the deceased is due to accidental injuries.
In the absence of specific medical records to show that he died of accidental injuries, it cannot be held that Nagappa died due to accidental injuries.
Though the PW3 has stated accidental injuries might have contributed the death of Nagappa, there is no documentary evidence to substantiate his version.

Therefore this tribunal has not given any importance to the oral testimony of PW3.
21.
The Petitioners have failed to prove the nexus between the accidental injuries and the death of original claimant.
He has not proved to be bed ridden or suffering with severe complications till his death.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative and Additional issue No.1 in the negative.
22. ISSUE NO.2:-

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue No.1 and additional issue No.1, I hold that Petitioners are entitled only for the medical expenses in view of the various decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court of Karnataka.

It is relevant to note in case of ILR 2020 KAR 357 wherein the Hon'ble High Court has held that the claim of the appellant seeking compensation for the death of Petitioner due to accident was not accepted and only the medical expenses must be awarded.

23. In the present case the LRs of the Petitioner have produced the medical bills at Ex.P.14,
amounting to 11,480/-.
the respondent no 2 insurance company has not disputed medical bills.
On perusal of all medical bills, all appears to be genuine and hence Petitioners are awarded 11,480/-.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
24. ADDITIONAL ISSUE NO.2:
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argued that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the offending car without possessing valid driving license.
Thereby the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners and respondent No.2- insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle and relied upon the decisions rendered in MFA.3288/2013 C/w 3287/2013 between M/s.Shriram Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., Vs. Mrs.Sunitha @ Nagaveni and others and another decision in MFA.3390/2015 between M/s. Tata AIG Gen. Ins.Co.Ltd., Vs. K.R.Prakash and another, wherein, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held in the said cases that the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation in case the driver of insured vehicle not possessing a valid driving license at the time of the accident.
25.

entities.text: Tata AIG Gen. Ins.Co.Ltd., Vs. K.R.Prakash and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case on hand the charge sheet shows that at the time of alleged accident the driver of offending vehicle did not possess a valid driving license.
In spite of claim notice, the respondent No.1 did not turn up before this court and has not resisted the application.

Therefore, whatever Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135304279/
6 defence taken by the respondent No.2 stands un-challenged.

entities.text: Nagappa Alias Nagraj vs Sathaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the tribunal concludes that the driver of offending vehicle did not have a valid and effective driving license at the time of alleged accident.

Therefore, the insurer is not liable to pay any compensation to the Lrs of the petitioners and the said insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.

26. Liability :. Though the policy of the offending vehicle was in force at the time of alleged accident,
as I have already discussed in detail in additional issue No.2 that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions incorporated in the policy and thereby the respondent No.2 is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.1-owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly I answer additional issue No.2 in the affirmative.
27. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above Issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of 11,480/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1-owner shall liable to pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with interest shall be disbursed in favour of wife of deceased i.e., Petitioner No.1 through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 11th day of November 2024.)
(SHYLA S.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACJM Member, MACT Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.
